html:
The Atsugewi are a Native people of northeastern California, near Mount Lassen and Mount Shasta, along Hat Creek, Burney Creek and Dixie Valley. They had two divisions, the Atsuge ("pine tree people") of Hat Creek and the Apwaruge ("juniper tree people") of Dixie Valley.

Their language was close to that of the Achomawi of the Pit River to the north; together they make up the Palaihnihan family. They lived by hunting deer, fishing, and gathering acorns, seeds and roots. The California Gold Rush and settlers who came after it broke up their life in the 1850s. Today they are part of the Pit River Tribe. Their neighbours included the Maidu to the south and the Shasta.
